outcome: Extended perinatal mortality (intrapartum stillbirths and neonatal deaths)
cohort: The study participants were pregnant women in Scotland at 24-36 gestational weeks with a singleton breech baby, no prior caesarean birth, in spontaneous labour with a live baby at labour onset between 1997 and 2019.
finding: Caesarean birth was associated with a reduced risk of extended perinatal mortality in spontaneous preterm singleton breech labour when compared to vaginal breech birth.
mod_finding: Caesarean birth significantly reduced extended perinatal mortality compared to vaginal breech birth, with the protective effect being more pronounced at earlier gestational ages.
followup_time: Up to 28 days post-birth (for neonatal deaths)
